newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK democrats question need for Chinese troops.
newsitem.headline: HK democrats question need for Chinese troops.

text.p: The leader of Hong Kong's democracy movement, Martin Lee, on Monday questioned the need for stationing Chinese troops in Hong Kong and said the territory's people were unhappy about the prospect.

Lee, leader of the Democratic Party, made the remarks as an advance party of 40 People's Liberation Army (PLA) soldiers arrived to prepare facilities for the garrison that will take over defence duties when Britain pulls out at midnight on June 30.
The unit drove into Hong Kong on Monday from China's border town of Shenzhen.
"The stationing of troops in Shenzhen would have been sufficient to protect Hong Kong if necessary," Lee told a news conference after returning from a lobbying tour of Europe and North America.
"The British garrison was stationed here for an obvious reason, that is in case there was an invasion from a certain direction," Lee said.
"But when Hong Kong is part of China there is no question of Hong Kong facing such a threat from the same direction and I don't see any threat of any foreign invasion," he said.
"I don't think Hong Kong people will feel too happy about the stationing of the troops.

"But I hope they will abide by both Hong Kong laws and mainland military laws in China...I hope the soldiers would by their conduct allay the fears that Hong Kong people may still have about them in Hong Kong," Lee said.

Fellow Democratic Party legislator Huang Chen-ya told Reuters Television that the PLA stirred up memories of the 1989 military crackdown against China's student-led democracy movement in Beijing's Tiananmen Square.

"Many People in Hong Kong have mixed feelings about the PLA, a lot of which is in fact fear. So the behaviour of the PLA, the first contingent of the PLA, in Hong Kong will certainly have an impact on how Hong Kong will see the arrival of the Chinese government and its representatives," Huang said.

"We know there is going to be a much larger contingent coming into Hong Kong after July 1, and so people will want to know whether the PLA people will in fact follow the law...and will not reflect the problems people saw during the Tiananmen incident."
